lines.li: [them] I've been here before, but never as a guest at your table.
[us] Then tonight you'll see the place at its best.
[them,their:tribal] Then I will eat like a guest and boast like one.
[them] Then I'll try to behave like a guest.
[us] You walked in with the guests, didn't you?
[them,their:tribal] Where I come from, a guest never walks to a feast alone.
[them,their:empire] I attend the guest of honor, and I eat when they have eaten.
[them,their:industrial] Somebody had to carry the bags, and I drew the short straw.
[them] Someone had to keep them company on the road, and I didn't argue.
[us] Well, you're as welcome here as they are.
[them] I'm told the contests start this afternoon.
[us] They do, and you'll get a fair field.
[them,their:spacer] Is there a written set of rules I could look over first?
[them,their:medieval] Then I'll find someone to hold my cloak.
[them] Then I'll save my strength until then.
[them] Rain, on the feast day of all days.
[us] It may clear yet.
[them,their:tribal] Our elders would say the sky wants a seat at the feast.
[them] If it doesn't, I'll eat just as well wet.
[them] Snow for the feast, then, and a cold walk home in it.
[us] Leave your boots inside the door, they'll be dry by supper.
[them] That's the best thing anyone's said to me all day.
[them] Hot day for a feast.
[us] The evening will be cooler, and that's when we eat.
[them] Then I'll save my appetite for the cool of it.
[us] Sit wherever you like tonight, we don't keep places here.
[them,their:empire] I would rather be shown my place, if it's all the same to you.
[them,their:tribal] Then I sit where the meat is closest.
[them] Then I'll sit near the cook and take my chances.
[us] Fair enough.
[them] Your people stay up late on a feast night.
[us] We don't often get the chance.
[them,their:medieval] At home the hall would be snoring by now.
[them] I'll be up at first light all the same, the road is long.
[them] Will there be prayers before the meal?
[us] Each says their own, if they want to.
[them] Then I'll say mine under my breath and not keep anyone waiting.
[them] It's good to sit down to a feast with people who share our faith.
[us] Then we'll give thanks together tonight.
[them] Gladly, and in the same words for once.
[them] At court, no evening is complete without music.
[us] We'll do what we can with what we have.
[them] That is all a guest of sense would ask.
[them] A titled host, out here, I shall tell them that at court.
[us] Tell them the food was good, they'll care more about that.
[them] You don't know the court.
[us] Will you be taking part, or watching?
[them] Watching, and telling the young ones what they're doing wrong.
[us] That's a contest of its own.
[us] That looks sore.
[them] It is, but I'm not going home early for it.
[us,colony:doctor] Let {DOCTOR} look at it before you set out tomorrow.
[us] Tell someone if it gets worse in the night.
[them] Your people pour a heavy cup.
[us] You don't have to finish it.
[them] I'll finish it, and I'll remember who poured it.
[them] I didn't walk all this way to be laughed at.
[us] Then sit with someone else.
[them] I'll remember this table when I'm home.
[us] Remember the cook, that's who did the work.
[them,their:medieval] Then the cook gets a toast, and so does the hall.
[them] Then here's to the cook.
[us,us:best:Cooking] That's me, and I'll take it.
[us] I'll tell them you said so.
[us] Do you know who's coming from your people?
[them,their:empire] Whoever holds the right rank for it, which settles the arguing.
[them] Whoever could be spared, and whoever argued loudest.
[us] We'll set enough places, whoever it is.
[them,their:tribal] Our young hunters have run every morning since your word came.
[them,their:industrial] Ours have been timing each other on the road with a pocket watch.
[them] Our people have been practicing for your contests.
[us] Ours too, though they'd never admit it.
[them] I hope the weather's kinder on your feast day.
[us] If it isn't, we wait for the first fine one.
[them] Then our people will wait with you.
[them] Your invitation was well written, for a frontier house.
[us] Then you'll come?
[them] I shall answer properly, in writing, as it should be done.
[them] Your messenger brought word of {FEAST}, and the elders are talking it over.
[us] Tell them we'd be honored.
[them] I'll tell them, and they'll take their time all the same.
[us] I don't think {FEAST} went the way we hoped.
[them] No, and our people noticed.
[us] We'll do better by you, if you'll give us the chance.
[them] Maybe.
[them] I was there when {CHAMPION} won, and I've told it a dozen times since.
[us] Has it grown in the telling?
[them] Only the part about how big the crowd was.
[them] {CHAMPION} beat us fairly, I'll say that for your people.
[us] And yours made {CHAMPION} work hard for it.
[them] We did, and we'll do it again next time.
[them] You lost to {CHAMPION} at your own feast.
[us] We did, and we'll live.
[them] So you will.
[them,trait:Brawler] Next time I want a go at {CHAMPION} myself, no rules.
[them] Next time I want a go at {CHAMPION} myself.
[us] {CHAMPION} will be glad of the practice.
[them] To hear our people tell it, {CHAMPION} could beat anyone in the region.
[us] {CHAMPION} would be glad to hear that.
[them] Don't pass it on, it'll go to their head.
[us] You were at {FEAST}, weren't you?
[them] I was, and I went home with a full belly and no voice left from cheering.
[us] Then you'll have to come back and lose it again.
[them] Your feast was a quiet one, and I liked it that way.
[us] No contests, just food and talk.
[them,old] At my age that's the better kind.
[them] The talk was the best part of it.
[them] I still remember sitting at your table with nothing in front of me.
[us] So do we, and we're sorry for it.
[them] Sorry doesn't fill a plate.
[them] You invited me to watch your people eat.
[us] That's not how it was meant.
[them] The elders still speak of {FEAST} in the evenings.
[us] I'm glad it's remembered.
[them] They say it was a feast the way the old ones held them.
[them] At our market they still talk about {FEAST}, and your cook.
[us] Our cook will be impossible to live with if I tell them.
[them] Then wait until we've gone.
[them] Word of {FEAST} has done your name more good than a season of trade.
[us] We'd rather have both.
[them] Then keep holding them, and keep trading.
[them] What we heard of {FEAST} wasn't all good.
[us] Some of it was our fault, I'll grant that.
[them] Granting it is a start.
[them] Will you hold another one next year?
[us] If the harvest allows it.
[them,their:spacer] Then I'd like to reserve a seat now.
[them] Then I hope the harvest is a good one.
[them] Our people still remember the feast your colony held for them.
[us] It was a good night, I remember it too.
[them,their:lowtech] A table like that is talked of for a generation.
[them] It still comes up whenever your colony's name does.
[them] Your people came to our feast when we asked, and that was remembered.
[us] We'd go again.
[them,their:tribal] Then come for the next great hunt, and bring a spear.
[them,their:medieval] Then come for the next tournament, and bring your best arm.
[them,their:industrial] Then come to the next fair, and bring something worth selling.
[them] Then you'll be asked again.
[them] We set places for your people at our feast, and they stayed empty.
[us] I'm sorry, we couldn't get there.
[them] Next time, send word if you can't come.
